requirement_text.ISS-0216: Letflow.Api.Pagination.decode_cursor/4 trusted its caller-supplied prefix with no non-empty guard -- check_prefix/2's size/starts_with? logic trivially passes when prefix is the empty string, since every decoded cursor starts with the empty string, defeating the cross-endpoint cursor isolation this parameter exists to provide. Real route handlers (audit.ex, tasks.ex, instances.ex, tenants.ex, identity.ex, definitions.ex) already call decode_cursor/4 with hardcoded non-empty module-attribute prefixes; the guard was still missing.

result.summary:
Scope test: this diff (git diff main...HEAD on lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex only, commit 2b0d881) adds one new leading defp check_prefix/2 clause matching prefix == "" that raises ArgumentError, plus moduledoc/@doc wording (INV-9 paragraph). It is a cross-endpoint cursor-isolation guard reachable from real route handlers (audit.ex, tasks.ex, instances.ex, tenants.ex, identity.ex, definitions.ex all call decode_cursor/4) -- in scope per the handoff's own framing; scope test run, not skipped, and would have flagged this in-scope even without that framing (INV-6/INV-8 both attach).

Per-invariant verdicts:

INV-1 (tenant data isolation, Ecto :prefix scoping) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. Verified: grepped the diff and the whole file for Repo/Ecto.Schema usage -- none (moduledoc itself states, unchanged by this diff, 'no Ecto.Schema/Repo call anywhere in this module'). No migration, no schema, no :prefix-scoped query touched. Pagination.ex is a pure encode/decode module; Cursor.t() has exactly one field (inner :: binary()), no tenant_id/schema/prefix slot (existing module-local INV-1/INV-5 doc, unchanged) -- there is no tenant-scoped table or query for this change to reach. INV-1 does not attach to this diff.

INV-2 (server-side field authorisation) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No API response type or field-serialisation code touched; check_prefix/2 raises before any response is built, and the diff adds no new response field.

INV-3 (untrusted runtime sandboxing) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No Lua/WASM/S5 code involved.

INV-4 (secrets by reference only) -- APPLIES (live now), PASS. Ran: grep -n "System.get_env\|password\|secret\|client_secret\|token" lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex -- zero hits. This diff introduces no secret material, no logging, no error-message field that could carry one; the ArgumentError message only names prefix (a hardcoded per-endpoint literal like "T:", never a secret).

INV-5 (not-found/forbidden indistinguishability) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No lookup-by-ID endpoint or response-shaping code touched; this is a pagination-cursor precondition guard, not an existence-check code path.

INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping) -- APPLIES, PASS. This handoff itself is the proof artifact: change traced end-to-end, invariants enumerated, verify procedures actually run (this document). check_prefix/2 is not a new data-access path (no new route, no new migration) but a tightening of an existing cross-endpoint isolation check reachable from six route-handler modules -- confirmed via grep that decode_cursor/4's only callers (audit.ex:225, tenants.ex:288, identity.ex:301/551, tasks.ex:653, instances.ex:260/321 -> decode_seq_cursor/2 at instances.ex:133/170, definitions.ex:1909/2077) all pass a compile-time module-attribute literal (@audit_cursor_prefix, @tenants_cursor_prefix, @users_cursor_prefix, @group_members_cursor_prefix, @list_cursor_prefix, @history_cursor_prefix, @timeline_cursor_prefix, @definitions_list_cursor_prefix, @definitions_search_cursor_prefix) -- none derive prefix from request/query/path input, none pass "". The fix closes the gap for a future call site, without altering any existing call site's behavior.

INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. Ran: grep -n "Repo.query" lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex -- zero hits. No SQL in this module at all.

INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) -- APPLIES, PASS (with explicit reasoning, since this diff's whole content is a new raise). INV-8's own scope, per its Rule text, is 'any path that touches external I/O, tenant-controlled data, or network input' -- and per this module's own moduledoc (unchanged text, lines 26-29), 'cursor/page-size values are caller-controlled, network-facing input' is exactly the class INV-8 protects against crashing. prefix is not in that class: verified by tracing every real caller (listed above under INV-6) -- all nine call sites pass a hardcoded, compile-time module-attribute string literal, never a value derived from Plug.Conn params, query string, path, or any other request-facing input. An empty prefix can only arise from a future call site's own source code, not from any external actor's request -- this is a caller-contract/programmer-error precondition (the same class Keyword.fetch!/2, Map.fetch!/2 raise on), not the 'realistic failure path on network input' INV-8 exists to prevent. Confirmed no realistic external input can trigger the new raise: grep -rn \"decode_cursor(\" lib/ shows zero call sites constructing prefix from request data. Also ran the module-wide INV-8 heuristic grep: grep -n "^\s*{:ok, .*} = " lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex -- zero hits (no bare pattern match introduced). mix test test/letflow/api/pagination_test.exs: 'Finished in 0.1 seconds ... Result: 38 passed', 0 failures -- confirms no non-empty-prefix path's behavior changed.

Supporting verification, both commands run directly (not trusted from ELIXIR-DEV's report): mix format --check-formatted lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex -> exit 0, no diff. mix compile --warnings-as-errors -> exit 0, no warnings.

No invariant failed. No open question from the design's §5 changes this verdict -- §5's two flagged alternatives (a {:error, :invalid_prefix} tuple instead of raise; guarding non-binary prefix) are design choices already reasoned through against INV-8 in the design doc and independently re-verified above, not defects.

invariant_verdicts.INV-1: NOT-APPLICABLE -- no Ecto schema/migration/query touched, pure encode/decode module
invariant_verdicts.INV-2: NOT-APPLICABLE -- no API response/field-serialisation code touched
invariant_verdicts.INV-4: APPLIES -- PASS (grep clean, no secret material introduced)
invariant_verdicts.INV-6: APPLIES -- PASS (this handoff is the proof artifact; all call sites traced and confirmed hardcoded)
invariant_verdicts.INV-7: NOT-APPLICABLE -- no SQL in this module
invariant_verdicts.INV-8: APPLIES -- PASS (raise is on caller-contract/programmer-error input, not network-facing input; all 9+ call sites verified hardcoded; 38/38 existing tests pass unchanged)
